Abdin Pharmacies retain the rights established by law in the management, organization and development of their electronic services, take appropriate action to prevent their misuse and protect their clients, employees, installations and legitimate interests.

10. External service provider: any independent party contributing to the operation of payment, shipping, hosting, technical or other site-related services.
The terms are interpreted in accordance with the nature of the transaction and the provisions of the Egyptian law in force.

section.h2: Article 6: Lawful Use of the Website
section.p: The user is committed to using the site only for legitimate purposes, in accordance with Egyptian laws, public morals and the rights of others.
In particular, it is prohibited:
1. Attempt unauthorized access to site regulations or databases.
2. Use harmful programmes or technical means that threaten the integrity of the site.

Appropriate action may be taken to stop any unlawful activity, including restricting access to services or notifying the competent authorities where there is a legal requirement.
The site aims to facilitate client access to information, services and products provided by Abdin Pharmacies.

Services may include providing information on products, receiving inquiries, verifying availability, managing requests, identifying payment and delivery options and providing means of communicating with customer service.
Inclusion of a product on site does not necessarily mean that it is available for purchase or delivery at all times or in all regions.
Nor does its electronic presentation mean that it may be disbursed without meeting its legal and pharmaceutical requirements.
Actual service is subject to the availability of products, the validity of licences, regulatory requirements, implementation possibilities and restrictions on the handling of certain items.
The site may contain health, pharmaceutical or tariff information on products, including common uses, components, warnings, precautions and general instructions.

Published information is provided for purposes of definition and awareness, and may not be considered an automatic alternative to individual medical diagnosis, clinical examination or description of treatment by specialists.

The product ' s suitability may vary from one person to another depending on age, state of health, sick history, pregnancy, breastfeeding, other medicines, sensitivity, vital functions and other medical considerations.

The user is required to consult the competent doctor or pharmacist before using the formulations that require it, and not rely on site information alone to make remedial decisions requiring professional evaluation.

Pharmacies shall not bear the consequences of the user ' s reliance on public information outside their context, or the use of a product in a manner contrary to stated guidance and warnings, unless such results are linked to a firm legal or professional breach by pharmacies.
The website is not a medical emergency reception facility and does not ensure an immediate response to urgent inquiries.

Communication or electronic conversations should not be used to request urgent medical intervention in cases such as severe respiratory difficulty, lack of awareness, acute chest pain, severe bleeding, stroke symptoms, poisoning, overdoses, excessive sensitivity, or any situation suspected of threatening life or requiring immediate intervention.
In such cases, an appropriate medical facility or liaison with the competent emergency services must be immediately approached.
The availability of an electronic communication service is not interpreted as an undertaking to provide emergency medical consultations or continuous clinical follow-up.
Pharmaceuticals give reasonable care to present product data as clearly and accurately as possible.
However, some packaging details, packaging designs or illustrative images may differ as a result of approved changes from manufacturers or product updates.

Official statements printed on the packaging and approved pamphlets are of fundamental importance in identifying user instructions, warnings and components, taking into account the supplier ' s obligation to provide accurate and uncontested information.

In the event of an influential difference in the effective substance, concentration, size or basic specifications, the rules of conformity and consumer rights are applied, and an alternative product may not be imposed on the client without the consent of the client where necessary.

Prices may change in the future as a result of modifications by producers, competent authorities or legitimate trade policies.

The client is not required to pay additional amounts that have not been properly approved, nor may payments made for an application not executed without the settlement of his rights in accordance with the law be retained.

Medicines may not be replaced or their basic specifications changed in a manner contrary to professional assets or regulations.

Applications containing restricted products are subject to review and the necessary documentation and requirements are met.

Pharmacies are obliged to make available material information on remote contracting, and methods of confirmation, correction and modification of the application, in accordance with the legal provisions of the Organization.
The client may be contacted to confirm the data, address the differences in availability or clarify information necessary for the execution of the request.
The conditions of final treatment must be clear to the client, while preserving his or her right to induce or amend when determined by law.
The offer of a pharmaceutical or the receipt of a request relating to it shall not entail the exemption of the client or the pharmacy from the requirements governing its discharge.
Pharmaceuticals retain the right and obligation to demand a proper and confidential prescription when required by law.

Products must be used in accordance with their purpose and the instructions and warnings adopted.

Pharmacies shall not bear the consequences exclusively of misuse, contravention of instructions or use of the product for its illicit purposes, without prejudice to any established legal liability.

Legal liability for the known and declared side effect of the formulation upon its proper use varies from liability arising from a product ' s defect, failure to conserve, process, provide or disburse the product.
Liability is determined in each case in accordance with applicable facts, evidence and laws.

section.h2: Article 25: General Exchange and Return Policy
section.p: Abdin Pharmacies respect the consumer ' s rights under the Egyptian Consumer Protection Act and its implementing regulations, including those relating to substitution, retrieval and discontinuation.

In general, consumers enjoy the right to replace and retrieve during legally prescribed periods, including the right to replace or retrieve within 14 days of receipt of the goods without reason, taking into account the legal exceptions relating to the nature and condition of certain goods.
Consumer also enjoys rights with respect to defective or non-conforming products, including rights established within 30 days of receipt, extensions and best or special guarantees when applicable.
This policy may not be interpreted as depriving the consumer of its legal rights.
Exceptions are applied according to the nature and circumstances of the product, the relevant legal texts and regulatory decisions.

section.h2: Article 26: Special Rules for Medicine Returns
section.p: Pharmaceuticals and products whose safety is affected by storage and handling conditions are subject to special controls that require the safety of patients and the quality of products.

The nature or characteristics of certain products, the manner in which they are mobilized or the requirements for their preservation may prevent their return from being accepted in cases where the exception is permitted by law.
In particular, consideration is given to whether the integrity of the product can be ascertained and not exposed to conditions affecting its viability or characteristics.
A renegotiation of a refrigerated formulation may be possible only if the legal and technical rules permit it.

This provision does not dismiss the client ' s right to claim compensation, replacement or recovery of value when there is a defect, failure or error in the execution of the application, where the requirements of the right are provided by law.
Each request for retrieval is evaluated according to the nature of the item, available evidence and regulatory controls.

section.h2: Article 27: How to Request a Return
section.p: The client may apply for replacement or retrieval through approved customer service channels.
It would be preferable to provide the number of demand or invoice, to describe the problem and information that would help to identify the product and treatment.
Explanatory photographs or examination of the product may be requested when needed, but this may not become an unlawful impediment to the exercise of legal rights.
Applications are examined according to the nature and duration of the problem.

In the event of a proven defect, error or non-conformity with a legal right to replace or retrieve, treatment measures shall be taken without charge to the consumer of costs for which the law prohibits them.
The application is not denied simply because the outer casing is not retained if the refusal is contrary to an existing legal right.
The amounts owed to the client are reimbursed in accordance with the laws governing the nature of the transaction and the means of payment used.
The payment shall be made in the same way as the original payment, unless the parties agree on another means of a law award.
The amounts assessed for reimbursement are taken into account, including provisions for remote contracting and returns of products.
Some e-recovery operations may require additional time to appear in the client ' s account as a result of the actions of the banker or payment service provider.
Pharmacies may not reserve a receivable of restitution without legal authority.

In the event of a disagreement as to the value or components of the amount, the client is available to communicate with the customer service and to provide the necessary documentation for the examination of the transaction.
The client may request that the request be amended or cancelled in accordance with the declared mechanisms and legal rights relating to remote contracting.
The possibility of operational adjustment may vary depending on the demand processing stage and the nature of the products.
The start-up or shipment of the request does not result in the loss of a client ' s statutory right to induce or retrieve.
Provisions relating to the right to rectify or modify a request and to refrain from contracting are applied in accordance with the Consumer Protection Act and its implementing regulations.
If a specific amendment cannot be implemented for legitimate reasons, the client shall be notified of the options available without prejudice to his or her rights.
Pharmacies retain the right to take appropriate action when there are serious indications of fraud or misuse.
Such cases may include the use of unauthorized means of payment, false statements, repeated fictitious requests for damage, or attempts to obtain illicitly restricted formulations.
The execution of the transaction may be suspended to the extent necessary to verify its legality, taking into account the legal rights of the client.
When an unlawful act of damage is established, pharmacists may claim their rights before the competent authorities.
These provisions may not be used to restrict legitimate complaints or to exercise the legal rights of consumers.

Data may not be used or disclosed in violation of the law.
The addressee is obliged to take the necessary regulatory and technical measures to protect the data and to enable its owners to exercise their legal rights.

section.p: Pharmacists seek to operate the site in a stable and secure manner, applying appropriate measures for the nature of the service.

The site may contain links to sites or services of independent parties, such as payment companies, manufacturers or technical service providers.
The reference to an external party does not imply the adoption of all its contents, policies or guarantees.
Independent services are subject to the requirements of their providers, to the extent that they do not conflict with the client ' s rights to be treated with pharmacies.
Pharmacies do not have responsibility for the content or practices of an independent external party that did not have control over it or a legal contribution to the damage caused.

section.h2: Article 39: No Guarantee of Individual Results
section.p: Pharmacies do not provide a general guarantee of a specific remedial or cosmetic result for each user simply to purchase a product from the site.
The results may vary depending on individual characteristics, method of use, state of health and other factors.
Public opinions or personal assessments published on a product, if any, are not conclusive evidence of access by all users to the same results.
Nor does general information explain the potential benefits of formulations as a personal promise of healing or improvement.
This does not prejudice the obligation of pharmacists not to publish misleading information or unaccredited remedial allegations, or their responsibility for any relevant legal offence.

section.h2: Article 40: Exceptional Circumstances and Force Majeure
section.p: Pharmacies are not liable for non-implementation or delay, which is established to be a direct result of force majeure or a foreign cause in which legal requirements are met.

Exceptional circumstances, depending on their nature and the applicability of force majeure clauses, may include natural disasters, emergency government decisions, public disturbances or severe malfunctions beyond control.
Pharmacies are obliged to take reasonable action to limit the effects of these circumstances when possible.
The occurrence of an exceptional circumstance does not entail the loss of consumer rights in the recovery of funds, termination of contract or claiming other rights when determined by law.

section.h2: Article 41: User Responsibility for Unlawful Acts
section.p: The user is obliged not to engage in unlawful acts that cause harm to pharmacies, their employees or other users.
If an employee is found to have committed an unlawful act resulting in direct harm, pharmacies may claim compensation in accordance with general legal rules.
This article is not interpreted as requiring the user to compensate pharmacies for merely filing a complaint, exercising a legal right or objecting to a transaction.
Nor are any liability imposed by law on pharmacies or their service providers transferred to the user.

The client can lodge a complaint through official communication channels posted on the site.
It would be preferable to include the number of requests, the description of the problem and any information or documents that would assist in its examination.
Complaints are reviewed in accordance with their nature and the relevant legal and professional obligations.
Client service procedures do not prevent consumers from resorting to the Consumer Protection Service, the Egyptian Medicine Authority or competent supervisory and judicial bodies.
Access to pharmacies ' consent is not required before the exercise of legal rights to file complaints or communications.

section.h2: Article 43: Updates and Changes to These Terms
section.p: Pharmacies may update these conditions and provisions from time to time to keep pace with operational, technical, regulatory or legal developments.
The updated version is advertised through the site, with its entry into force in accordance with legal requirements.
Amendments may not be applied retroactively to existing transactions if they result in a reduction in acquired rights or breaches of legal obligations.
The user is advised to review the requirements periodically, especially before new transactions are completed.

Pharmacies may keep transaction logs, requests, invoices, confirmation notices and correspondence to the extent and to the extent permitted or imposed by law.
These records may be used to establish business processes, to process complaints or to meet accounting and regulatory obligations.
Electronic records and methods of reference are subject to evidence, electronic signature and data protection.
This article does not deprive the client of providing counter-substantiation or challenging the validity or content of any record by legal means.
Transactions and services provided by Abdin Pharmacies within the Arab Republic of Egypt are subject to applicable Egyptian laws.
These laws include, depending on the nature of the transaction, consumer protection legislation, pharmacology, regulation of the handling of formulations, personal data and electronic transactions.

Disputes are brought to the attention of the competent judicial authorities by law, without prejudice to the established competences of the regulatory and administrative bodies or consumer protection rights.
This requirement does not include any prior waiver of jurisdiction or legal right that cannot be waived.

The doctor or pharmacist should also disclose the health information necessary to make a sound professional decision, while respecting personal data protection controls.
The response to formulations varies among individuals, and a unified remedial outcome or the absence of all side effects of each user cannot be guaranteed.
Pharmacies shall not bear the consequences exclusively of misuse, contravention of instructions or use of the product for its illicit purposes, without prejudice to any established legal liability.

Pharmacies shall not bear the consequences of the redistribution of medicines among family members or of giving them to an unintended person or the alteration of dose and duration after receipt contrary to the proper instructions, once the damage has been proved to have arisen exclusively from such behaviour and without prejudice to the duties of pharmacies in exchange, awareness and warning.
Some pharmaceuticals, cosmetics or health products may cause side effects or sensory interactions among some users.
Components and warnings must be reviewed before use, especially when there is a known history of sensitivity.
In the event of unusual symptoms, use should be discontinued when medical guidance so requires and appropriate professional advice.
Serious symptoms require urgent medical intervention.

Legal liability for the known and declared side effect of the formulation upon its proper use varies from liability arising from a product ' s defect, failure to conserve, process, provide or disburse the product.
Liability is determined in each case in accordance with applicable facts, evidence and laws.

section.h2: Article 25: General Exchange and Return Policy
section.p: Abdin Pharmacies respect the consumer ' s rights under the Egyptian Consumer Protection Act and its implementing regulations, including those relating to substitution, retrieval and discontinuation.

In general, consumers enjoy the right to replace and retrieve during legally prescribed periods, including the right to replace or retrieve within 14 days of receipt of the goods without reason, taking into account the legal exceptions relating to the nature and condition of certain goods.
Consumer also enjoys rights with respect to defective or non-conforming products, including rights established within 30 days of receipt, extensions and best or special guarantees when applicable.
This policy may not be interpreted as depriving the consumer of its legal rights.
Exceptions are applied according to the nature and circumstances of the product, the relevant legal texts and regulatory decisions.

The substitution and retrieval rules established shall be applied by law, taking into account the specific exceptions to the product ' s quality and condition, and in terms of origin, the consumer protection system shall reflect the consumer ' s right to return or replace the goods within fourteen days without reason, with exceptions, and the right to deal with defective goods within 30 days, without prejudice to better or special guarantees.

Recharge provisions may differ depending on the reason for restitution, the nature of the right exercised and the terms of the remote contract and the regulations. Where a defect has been established, a failure to conform or an error of pharmacies is established, the customer may not be charged expenses for which the charge is prohibited by law; the previous delivery fee is not used as a reason for withholding the value of a product for which the law requires payment.

section.h2: Article 26: Special Rules for Medicine Returns
section.p: Pharmaceuticals and products whose safety is affected by storage and handling conditions are subject to special controls that require the safety of patients and the quality of products.

The nature or characteristics of certain products, the manner in which they are mobilized or the requirements for their preservation may prevent their return from being accepted in cases where the exception is permitted by law.
In particular, consideration is given to whether the integrity of the product can be ascertained and not exposed to conditions affecting its viability or characteristics.
A renegotiation of a refrigerated formulation may be possible only if the legal and technical rules permit it.

This provision does not dismiss the client ' s right to claim compensation, replacement or recovery of value when there is a defect, failure or error in the execution of the application, where the requirements of the right are provided by law.
Each request for retrieval is evaluated according to the nature of the item, available evidence and regulatory controls.

Some formulations are not suitable for return to the circulation cycle after they are transferred to the client ' s possession if the circumstances of their preservation cannot be verified, and any treatment of drug residues shall be subject to the controls of the Egyptian medicine authority and the professional and organizational rules of each category; the exception to the restitution of medicine may not be circulated as an absolute prohibition of each claim relating to exchange error, defect or non-conformity.

In the event of cancellation or non-execution of the request prior to delivery, the settlement differs from the attempt to return a formulation received; it takes into account whether the value has already been obtained, whether the service has been performed, and what is required by law to reimburse or recalculate amounts.

section.h2: Article 27: How to Request a Return
section.p: The client may apply for replacement or retrieval through approved customer service channels.
It would be preferable to provide the number of demand or invoice, to describe the problem and information that would help to identify the product and treatment.
Explanatory photographs or examination of the product may be requested when needed, but this may not become an unlawful impediment to the exercise of legal rights.
Applications are examined according to the nature and duration of the problem.

In the event of a proven defect, error or non-conformity with a legal right to replace or retrieve, treatment measures shall be taken without charge to the consumer of costs for which the law prohibits them.
The application is not denied simply because the outer casing is not retained if the refusal is contrary to an existing legal right.

An enforcement or delivery complaint may be examined on the basis of demand data, notices, invoices, delivery records and damage photographs where necessary, and pharmacies do not require evidence that the consumer cannot reasonably obtain if a legal right is impaired.

Pharmaceuticals may examine communications alleging non-access, deficiency or incorrect receipt of an item, reconcile the data with the records of the branch, the delegate and the propellant, while preserving the client ' s right to resort to the competent authorities without requiring prior internal settlement.
The amounts owed to the client are reimbursed in accordance with the laws governing the nature of the transaction and the means of payment used.
The payment shall be made in the same way as the original payment, unless the parties agree on another means of a law award.
The amounts assessed for reimbursement are taken into account, including provisions for remote contracting and returns of products.
Some e-recovery operations may require additional time to appear in the client ' s account as a result of the actions of the banker or payment service provider.
Pharmacies may not reserve a receivable of restitution without legal authority.

In the event of a disagreement as to the value or components of the amount, the client is available to communicate with the customer service and to provide the necessary documentation for the examination of the transaction.

If the application cannot be fully implemented owing to the depletion of a item or the impossibility of a project in the supply, the interruption of the delivery service or a foreign cause, the original financial adjustment of the unimplemented application includes the restitution of previously collected products or services that have not been provided, in accordance with the terms and means prescribed by law; if a portion of the request is executed, the amounts due shall be calculated for the refund of the unimplemented portion after the receipt has been properly stated independent fee has been shown.

To the extent permitted by law, pharmacies are not considered as guarantors for any hypothetical benefit or alleged commercial profit as a result of the non-completion of an ordinary application, nor does an automatic obligation to pay additional compensation arise simply because of a request cancelled for reasons beyond their control, but the consideration of payment as a fundamental settlement does not exclude compensation, reimbursement of expenses, any sanction or other right established by law if the cause of entitlement is established, and does not limit liability for the safety or serious breach of the patient.

Refunds take into account whether the financial deduction has already been made or is merely a bank authorization or reservation not completed, and the duration of its appearance in the account may depend on paid procedures with the obligation of pharmacies to carry out the procedures to which they are subject by law.
The client may request that the request be amended or cancelled in accordance with the declared mechanisms and legal rights relating to remote contracting.
The possibility of operational adjustment may vary depending on the demand processing stage and the nature of the products.
The start-up or shipment of the request does not result in the loss of a client ' s statutory right to induce or retrieve.
Provisions relating to the right to rectify or modify a request and to refrain from contracting are applied in accordance with the Consumer Protection Act and its implementing regulations.
If a specific amendment cannot be implemented for legitimate reasons, the client shall be notified of the options available without prejudice to his or her rights.

Items may not be modified after processing or dispatching for operational reasons, but legal rights relating to remote contracting, delay, non-delivery and recovery remain in place where applicable; a request that has not met a legal requirement, is not possible to provide or has shown serious fraud indicators, with notice of the customer and settlement of outstanding payments may be cancelled.

If the client requests that the place of delivery be changed after the cost is approved, this may require a new account of the transportation fee in accordance with the branch ' s policy, the client ' s acceptance is required prior to the receipt of the increase, and the refusal of the adjusted wage does not result in automatic loss of the client ' s rights for payment or expenses to be reimbursed by the law.
Pharmacies retain the right to take appropriate action when there are serious indications of fraud or misuse.
Such cases may include the use of unauthorized means of payment, false statements, repeated fictitious requests for damage, or attempts to obtain illicitly restricted formulations.
The execution of the transaction may be suspended to the extent necessary to verify its legality, taking into account the legal rights of the client.
When an unlawful act of damage is established, pharmacists may claim their rights before the competent authorities.
These provisions may not be used to restrict legitimate complaints or to exercise the legal rights of consumers.

Unauthorized payment requests, intentional incorrect addresses or repeated requests for decommissioning may be treated with caution, and records may be consulted to establish facts; these provisions shall not be interpreted as allowing pharmacies to punish an agent simply for repeating a legitimate complaint or rejecting an unaccepted fee.
Abdin Pharmacies respect the privacy and personal data of users of their location.
Services may require the collection and processing of some data necessary to implement requests, communication, accounting or legal obligations.

Data are dealt with at the borders, purposes and legal bases established under the relevant Egyptian legislation, in particular the Personal Data Protection Act No. 151 of 2020 and its implementing regulations.
Data may not be used or disclosed in violation of the law.
The addressee is obliged to take the necessary regulatory and technical measures to protect the data and to enable its owners to exercise their legal rights.
Details of data collection, processing, retention, disclosure and rights of authors are subject to applicable legal provisions and disclosures of privacy.

Data necessary to assign the request to a branch, organize the route of the delivery delegate, communicate with the client, prove delivery or recover payment may be processed within the prescribed legal purposes and grounds, and data on prescriptions or health cases may be used for marketing or participation for other purposes only where the law permits and meets its requirements.
Some requests or inquiries may include information of a healthy nature, such as prescriptions, formulation names or data on the satisfactory situation.
Such information shall be subject to the protection of sensitive personal data when applicable to it by legal description.
Such data shall be collected, used, maintained or shared only in accordance with the grounds, approvals, licences and permits required by law.
It must be limited to persons authorized and to the extent necessary for the performance of their legitimate functions.
The transmission of health information to the site does not automatically allow the user to be used for any marketing or commercial purpose not related to the required service.
Children ' s statements and parents ' consent shall be taken into account whenever necessary.
The site may use attachment identification files and similar techniques for operational, security or analytical purposes or to improve user experience, depending on the techniques actually used.
The use of these techniques is subject to the requirements of notification, approval and selections established by law.

The categories of these techniques, their use and duration of retention and their associates are subject to legal controls and relevant privacy disclosures.
General consent to conditions and conditions may not be used as a substitute for separate consent when such consent is required by law.
Pharmaceuticals may send notices concerning requests, payments, delivery, retrieval, account security or operational matters necessary for the implementation of the transaction.
Promotional messages and marketing presentations are subject to relevant legal approvals and controls.

section.h2: Article 35: Website Security and Service Availability
section.p: Pharmacists seek to operate the site in a stable and secure manner, applying appropriate measures for the nature of the service.
However, temporary interruptions may occur as a result of maintenance, technical updates, malfunctions, electronic attacks or conditions beyond reasonable control.
The provision of the site is not an undertaking to ensure its uninterrupted operation at all times.
Maintenance, updates or temporary suspension of certain functions may be carried out to protect regulations or improve performance.

Pharmacies shall not bear losses arising exclusively from interruptions beyond their legal and actual control, to the extent permitted by law, without prejudice to their liability for any fixed default or obligations existing towards customers.

The synchronization of e-commerce information with branch regulations, delivery company records or propellant may be delayed, which explains the possibility of an unfinished request or offering a different indicative fee; pharmacies address the conflicting situation by reviewing the actual situation and informing the client of the correct data before it is obligated to do so and correct the error without dropping the effect of any binding contractual confirmation.
The site may contain links to sites or services of independent parties, such as payment companies, manufacturers or technical service providers.
The reference to an external party does not imply the adoption of all its contents, policies or guarantees.
Independent services are subject to the requirements of their providers, to the extent that they do not conflict with the client ' s rights to be treated with pharmacies.
Pharmacies do not have responsibility for the content or practices of an independent external party that did not have control over it or a legal contribution to the damage caused.
This regulation does not prejudice any liability established by law for pharmacies to select service providers or their work or to breach their consumer obligations.

Delivery may be accomplished by a branch delegate, an independent transporter or a technical service provider who organizes trips; it does not mean that all the responsibilities of the supplier are transferred automatically; responsibilities are determined depending on contracts, facts and legal rules, in particular those relating to the safety of formulations and consumer rights.

Pharmacies do not ensure that there is no incidental circumstance beyond their control by an independent party, but they are bound by the law ' s appropriate selection, reasonable procedures, follow-up and settlement of requests; in turn, they are not responsible for acts separate from the transaction that are not attributable to them by law, provided that the dispute is decided by evidence and by law.

The content shall not be copied, redisseminated or commercially exploited without a permit or legal authority.
The use of the site does not give the user any ownership or commercial licence in the labels or protected materials.
Information available for legitimate personal use may be used within the limits permitted by law.
Pharmacies retain the right to take appropriate legal action to protect their markings, content and legitimate rights.

Abdin Pharmacies are bound by the law ' s responsibilities for the safety and conformity of products, storage, circulation, exchange and delivery, consumer protection and personal data, and any other applicable obligations.
To the extent permitted by the law, pharmacies are not liable for damages found to have arisen exclusively from:
1. intentional use of products in contravention of proper instructions and warnings.
2. Incorrect or misleading material information provided by the user.
3. Use of formulations by persons not assigned to them in violation of medical controls.
4. Modification of packagings or tampering with contents of products after delivery.
5. Poor storage after the transfer of possession to the client.
6. Unlawful use of the account as a result of an independent act of the user or other, with no breach of the duty of proof by pharmacies.
7. External circumstances that cannot reasonably be expected or paid, if the conditions of the foreign cause are legally available.

The limits of liability set forth in this article do not apply to situations where exemption or restriction is prohibited by law, including responsibilities arising from a product ' s defect, failure to conserve, trade or breach of legal and professional obligations where the requirements are met.

If a product cannot be provided because of the depletion or exclusion of inventory for lack of safety, network failure, regulatory restriction or force majeure that meets the legal requirements and is not supplied to the client, the treatment of the amount paid for the non-implemented part shall be the basic financial obligation in cases where no other liability is established; pharmacies shall not be obliged to ensure that the customer obtains an unavailable product or seizes it from an illicit source or to compensate claims without legal support.

Such limits of liability, however, are not a general exemption from professional errors, delivery of defective producer, concealment of fees, non-payments or breach of obligations to declare prices or a peremptory obligation; if a fixed error entails damage to which the law requires reparation, the legal provisions are applied, and a general condition of the site cannot invalidate the client ' s right to compensation.

Pharmacies shall not be liable solely for damages arising from the intentional filing of an intentional wrong address or the rejection of a project for the delivery or mispreservation of the product after receipt or abuse, if the reasons for the absence of legal liability are available, and the burden of proof shall be borne by the claimant or the other party, in accordance with applicable rules, without the unlawful reversal of the burden of proof on the consumer.

section.h2: Article 39: No Guarantee of Individual Results
section.p: Pharmacies do not provide a general guarantee of a specific remedial or cosmetic result for each user simply to purchase a product from the site.
The results may vary depending on individual characteristics, method of use, state of health and other factors.
Public opinions or personal assessments published on a product, if any, are not conclusive evidence of access by all users to the same results.
Nor does general information explain the potential benefits of formulations as a personal promise of healing or improvement.
This does not prejudice the obligation of pharmacists not to publish misleading information or unaccredited remedial allegations, or their responsibility for any relevant legal offence.

section.h2: Article 40: Exceptional Circumstances and Force Majeure
section.p: Pharmacies are not liable for non-implementation or delay, which is established to be a direct result of force majeure or a foreign cause in which legal requirements are met.

Exceptional circumstances, depending on their nature and the applicability of force majeure clauses, may include natural disasters, emergency government decisions, public disturbances or severe malfunctions beyond control.
Pharmacies are obliged to take reasonable action to limit the effects of these circumstances when possible.
The occurrence of an exceptional circumstance does not entail the loss of consumer rights in the recovery of funds, termination of contract or claiming other rights when determined by law.

The sequence of requests may affect conditions such as large-scale disruption of electricity or communications, closure of roads, natural disasters, urgent formal decisions, severe disruptions to transport or interruption of supply for reasons beyond reasonable control; not all of these are automatically force majeure; rather, the extent to which they meet the requirements of the foreign cause and their real impact on the treatment is considered.

When the reason for the project to implement the application is finally prevented, pharmacies shall report to the client as far as possible and take steps to reimburse the unimplemented part or agree on a legitimate alternative, and shall not invoke the exceptional circumstance of maintaining an exchange for goods that have not been delivered without legal authority or for the termination of jus cogens.

section.h2: Article 41: User Responsibility for Unlawful Acts
section.p: The user is obliged not to engage in unlawful acts that cause harm to pharmacies, their employees or other users.
If an employee is found to have committed an unlawful act resulting in direct harm, pharmacies may claim compensation in accordance with general legal rules.
This article is not interpreted as requiring the user to compensate pharmacies for merely filing a complaint, exercising a legal right or objecting to a transaction.
Nor are any liability imposed by law on pharmacies or their service providers transferred to the user.
Pharmacies are obliged to provide an appropriate means of receiving client complaints and inquiries regarding products, services and transactions.
The client can lodge a complaint through official communication channels posted on the site.
It would be preferable to include the number of requests, the description of the problem and any information or documents that would assist in its examination.
Complaints are reviewed in accordance with their nature and the relevant legal and professional obligations.
Client service procedures do not prevent consumers from resorting to the Consumer Protection Service, the Egyptian Medicine Authority or competent supervisory and judicial bodies.
Access to pharmacies ' consent is not required before the exercise of legal rights to file complaints or communications.

The subjects of the complaints include the difference in the actual remuneration for delivery from the site, the absence of additional charges, the absence of access by the delegate, the lack of items, apparent or hidden damage, or the delay in the payment of a payment, and the complaint is examined by reference to invoice, demand data, confirmations, available correspondence and relevant evidence.

The client is not required to accept a settlement which is less than his legal right in exchange for simply receiving his complaint and does not prevent any operational restriction from filing a complaint with the Consumer Protection Service, the Egyptian Medicine Authority or the competent authority.

section.h2: Article 43: Updates and Changes to These Terms
section.p: Pharmacies may update these conditions and provisions from time to time to keep pace with operational, technical, regulatory or legal developments.
The updated version is advertised through the site, with its entry into force in accordance with legal requirements.
Amendments may not be applied retroactively to existing transactions if they result in a reduction in acquired rights or breaches of legal obligations.
The user is advised to review the requirements periodically, especially before new transactions are completed.
In cases where the law requires new approval or specific notification, pharmacies are bound by due process.

The policy of calculating fees for deliveries, areas or means of reimbursement available to future requests can be changed, with substantive updates being published and duly disclosed; a general amendment declaration is not used to reprimand a completed application without the necessary bond or approval, nor to change the rights of retrieval that arose prior to the amendment.
Pharmacies may keep transaction logs, requests, invoices, confirmation notices and correspondence to the extent and to the extent permitted or imposed by law.
These records may be used to establish business processes, to process complaints or to meet accounting and regulatory obligations.
Electronic records and methods of reference are subject to evidence, electronic signature and data protection.
This article does not deprive the client of providing counter-substantiation or challenging the validity or content of any record by legal means.

The application numbers generated by the site may differ from the invoices issued by the branches and from the payment and transportation references, and may be administratively linked to establish the course of the transaction; the different number of the document does not preclude the proof of the transaction, nor does the registry of the application on the site make an alternative to a legally binding invoice if its data are not met.

Where the value of the delivery fee is different in the site summary and the branch ' s invoice, the letters presented to the client and the statements before them, the nature of the confirmation and the requirements of the law shall be reviewed. The bill adopted shall be considered as an important record of settlement, without having any effect on correcting a fee that the client has not consented to or dismissing a right arising from a binding offer or contract.
Transactions and services provided by Abdin Pharmacies within the Arab Republic of Egypt are subject to applicable Egyptian laws.
These laws include, depending on the nature of the transaction, consumer protection legislation, pharmacology, regulation of the handling of formulations, personal data and electronic transactions.

Disputes are brought to the attention of the competent judicial authorities by law, without prejudice to the established competences of the regulatory and administrative bodies or consumer protection rights.
This requirement does not include any prior waiver of jurisdiction or legal right that cannot be waived.

Items relating to electronic sale, delivery, fees and discards shall be read, in particular, in the light of the Consumer Protection Act No. 181 of 2018, its implementing regulations and the relevant rules, in a manner not inconsistent with the provisions of the Egyptian Medicine Authority and the competent regulatory bodies, and the general wording shall not give priority to an internal policy on a legally binding or regulatory decision.

If it is found that one of the provisions of this document is ineffective, invalid or contrary to a legal order, this does not automatically invalidate the other provisions that can be applied independently and legitimately.
The provision in question shall be interpreted and applied to the extent permitted by law, without creating new obligations contrary to the will of the parties or the legal rules.
This principle may not be used to maintain a requirement that is unjust or contrary to consumer rights established by law.
Failure to exercise pharmacies of any right established by law on a given occasion is not a permanent waiver of this right.

Any settlement or waiver of a right is applicable only in accordance with the conditions and forms required by law.

section.h2: Article 48: Patient and Customer Safety First
section.p: Abdin Pharmacies place the safety of patients and clients as a fundamental consideration in the delivery of their services.
Therefore, it may make a legitimate professional or regulatory decision to suspend or reject the exchange of a producer when there are legal or pharmaceutical grounds for doing so.
No electronic request or payment process may be interpreted as an obligation to dispose of a formulation in violation of the law or professional assets.
In such cases, payments and unimplemented requests are dealt with in accordance with the client ' s legal rights.

If the expected speed of delivery is in conflict with the safety requirements of a pharmaceutical, safety and professional compliance shall be a priority. Pharmacies may suspend transmission, request receipt from the branch or arrange an appropriate means, indicating options and adjusting the value as required by law, without an unlawful undertaking of a remedial outcome or an untimely date.

These conditions and provisions represent the general framework for the use and handling of the website, together with the policies of privacy, replacement, retrieval, delivery and any special conditions clearly declared prior to contracting.
This document is applied in accordance with Egyptian laws, consumer protection provisions and professional and regulatory rules.
No provision may be interpreted as authorizing unauthorized activity, depriving the consumer of a legal right, or exempting from liability from which the law does not permit exemption.

These conditions are aimed at regulating the contractual relationship, at clarifying rights and obligations, at protecting electronic transactions against misuse and at facilitating the clear and fair handling of disputes.

In cases of non-implementation where no other liability is established, reimbursement of payments due for service or non-executed product shall be the basis for financial adjustment; this shall not preclude any established right of the consumer or liability that cannot be agreed to forfeiture; these provisions shall aim at delineating the de facto operational limits of the services, in compliance with the laws and regulations in force in the Arab Republic of Egypt.

Using or through the website of Abdin Pharmacies, the user acknowledges that it has had access to these conditions and provisions, and understands the nature of the services, products and legal and professional constraints involved.
